Subjective: Oreo, a 5-year-old male Labrador, has been lethargic and less playful for the past week. He shows reluctance to wake up and has difficulty walking, with an unusual posture and whining when moving. He usually plays about 2 hours daily but now only about 30 minutes. He is vaccinated and dewormed recently but has not had recent tick and flea control. He is fed home-cooked meals (rice and sambar) twice daily and is obese.
Objective: Physical examination revealed no significant neurological deficits. Ortolani test (ultralining test) was positive indicating hip joint laxity. Suspected hip dysplasia and possible patellar luxation. Radiographs (anteroposterior, lateral views) and spine imaging recommended to confirm diagnosis and rule out spinal involvement. Oreo is obese, which may exacerbate joint issues.
Assessment: Oreo likely has hip dysplasia with possible patellar luxation contributing to his clinical signs of lethargy, abnormal posture, and walking difficulty. Obesity is a significant contributing factor increasing joint stress. Early management is critical to prevent progression to arthritis.
Plan:
1. Initiate flea and tick control with options including Florina (Bravitu), fibroblan and esmetopril, saralana, moxeduct imidogloprid, or salamitin; Florina preferred.
2. Schedule radiographs to measure Norberg angle and assess hip and stifle joints plus spine.
3. Prescribe Spirocoxin for pain management.
4. Prescribe Contraway Force Etching joint supplement and omega 3, omega 6 fatty acids to reduce inflammation and improve joint health.
5. Implement obesity diet for weight reduction.
6. Advise physiotherapy including sit-stand-step exercises and swimming; avoid high-impact activities.
7. Monitor clinical response and consider surgical intervention (femoral head and neck ostectomy) if needed in future.
8. Provide written physiotherapy instructions.
9. Follow up for reassessment and weight monitoring.
Conclusion: Oreo is diagnosed with probable hip dysplasia and possible patellar luxation exacerbated by obesity. Early medical management, weight control, and physiotherapy are essential to improve quality of life and delay progression. Diagnostic imaging is required for confirmation and further treatment planning.
DifferentialDiagnosis: Hip dysplasia, patellar luxation, spinal issues causing neurological pain or gait abnormalities, arthritis secondary to joint degeneration.
KeyIssues: Lethargy, reluctance to move, abnormal posture, walking difficulty, obesity, positive Ortolani test, lack of recent tick and flea control.
AbnormalFindings: Positive Ortolani test indicating hip joint laxity, obesity, abnormal posture, reluctance to move, whining on movement.

Monitor Oreo's activity and report any worsening signs immediately.

Joint supplementation with Contraway Force Etching and omega fatty acids. Weight management diet protocol until ideal body condition achieved. Physiotherapy exercises daily with instructions provided. Radiographic evaluation protocol including anteroposterior, lateral, and spinal views.
